findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: Structured logging is active via AWS Lambda Powertools with client_id and correlation_id on every write operation. X-Ray tracing is enabled. However, no immutable or tamper-evident log storage is configured. CloudWatch Logs can be deleted by any principal with logs:DeleteLogGroup permission.
findings.gap: Logs exist and contain principal attribution, but are not stored immutably. No tamper-evident log mechanism is configured.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch Logs retention policy and configure log export to S3 bucket with Object Lock (compliance mode). Enable CloudTrail data events for the DynamoDB table.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND no immutable log storage configured
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: AUTH-Q6 is a conditional BLOCKER when agent_scope is write-enabled. This payments API exposes write operations (charges, refunds) and logs contain principal attribution, but the logs are not immutable — CloudWatch Logs can be deleted without Object Lock.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add CloudWatch Logs retention policy to SAM template and configure S3 export with Object Lock
blocker_remediation.target_state: All agent-initiated write operations logged immutably with principal attribution and tamper-evident storage

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: The system processes financial transaction data (payment charges and refunds). No data residency policy, compliance documentation, or cross-region data flow safeguards are documented or configured. The API Gateway uses a REGIONAL endpoint but no explicit controls prevent agent-to-LLM data transmission across jurisdictions.
findings.gap: No documented data residency requirements. No compliance markers. No technical safeguards for agent-to-LLM data transmission boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Document applicable data residency and compliance requirements. Add data handling boundary documentation specifying which fields an agent may transmit externally.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled AND financial transaction data with no residency policy
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q2 is a conditional BLOCKER when agent_scope is write-enabled. This payments system handles financial transaction data and has no documented residency requirements or safeguards for cross-jurisdiction data flow to LLM providers.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Document applicable data residency and compliance requirements for the payments data
blocker_remediation.target_state: Explicit residency policy with technical safeguards preventing unauthorized cross-region data transmission

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: The system authenticates machine clients via OAuth2 client-credentials flow. The authorizer extracts client_id and scopes but there is no mechanism to distinguish between an agent acting under its own service identity vs. acting on behalf of a specific human user.
findings.gap: No identity propagation or delegation mechanism. All requests are attributed to the machine client only.
findings.recommendation: Implement token exchange or on-behalf-of flow in the Lambda authorizer to carry user context when an agent operates on behalf of a human.

compensating_controls: Restrict agent scope to operations that do not require user-level attribution
Add X-On-Behalf-Of header support with validation

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: The system uses Cognito for OAuth2 token issuance and a Lambda authorizer for validation. No explicit suspension mechanism is configured in the repository for immediate agent identity revocation.
findings.gap: No in-repo mechanism or documented procedure for immediately suspending a specific agent identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement a deny-list check in the Lambda authorizer that can be updated dynamically via DynamoDB or Parameter Store.

compensating_controls: Use Cognito console to disable app client manually
Add client_id to deny list in Lambda authorizer

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: The _idempotent_put function performs a get_item followed by put_item without a DynamoDB ConditionExpression. Two concurrent requests with the same Idempotency-Key could both observe no existing record and both write, resulting in inconsistent state.
findings.gap: No conditional writes or optimistic locking on the idempotency check. Race condition window between get_item and put_item.
findings.recommendation: Add ConditionExpression='attribute_not_exists(pk)' to the idempotency record put_item call and handle ConditionalCheckFailedException.

compensating_controls: Use DynamoDB ConditionExpression for atomic check-and-write
Wrap get+put in DynamoDB TransactWriteItems

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: No explicit rate limiting or throttling configuration is defined in the SAM template. No API Gateway usage plans, no throttle settings, no WAF rate rules. The API relies on default API Gateway account-level throttling which is shared and not per-client.
findings.gap: No per-client rate limiting configured.
findings.recommendation: Define an AWS::ApiGateway::UsagePlan resource in template.yaml with per-client throttle rates.

compensating_controls: Add API Gateway UsagePlan with per-API-key throttling
Deploy AWS WAF with rate-based rules

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No configurable business-level transaction limits exist. An agent can issue unlimited refunds or create unlimited charges without any per-caller caps on business impact.
findings.gap: No per-caller business transaction limits. An agent error could issue thousands of refunds without bound.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable per-client business limits (max_refund_amount_per_day, max_charges_per_hour) enforced in the handler.

compensating_controls: Implement per-client_id refund count/amount limits
Add daily aggregate check before processing refunds

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: The Charge schema defines a status enum with pending/succeeded/failed, indicating the data model supports a pending state. However, the implementation sets status directly to 'succeeded' — no intermediate reviewable state is used.
findings.gap: No draft or pending workflow is active. Schema supports it but implementation bypasses it.
findings.recommendation: Implement a two-step flow where charges are created with status='pending' and require explicit confirmation.

compensating_controls: Modify create_charge to use pending state with separate confirm endpoint
Implement orchestration-layer approval gate

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No configurable approval gates exist. All operations execute immediately upon API call. No Step Functions with human approval tasks or operation-level flags to require confirmation.
findings.gap: No mechanism to require human approval before high-value operations.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable amount thresholds that route high-value operations through an approval workflow.

compensating_controls: Implement threshold-based approval in agent orchestration layer
Add Step Function workflow with waitForTaskToken for high-value refunds

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: OpenAPI spec is versioned (1.4.0), API uses URL versioning (/v1/), and spec is validated in CI. However, no breaking change detection tool is configured.
findings.gap: No automated breaking change detection between spec versions.
findings.recommendation: Add oasdiff or similar OpenAPI comparison tool to CI that fails the build on breaking changes.

compensating_controls: Add oasdiff to CI pipeline
Implement consumer-driven contract tests

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: RUNBOOK.md documents alarms (payments-5xx >1% over 5min, idempotency-conflict >10/min, ddb-throttle) but these are not defined in IaC.
findings.gap: Alarms documented but not codified in IaC. No guarantee they are deployed.
findings.recommendation: Define documented alarms as AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm resources in template.yaml.

compensating_controls: Add CloudWatch Alarm resources to SAM template
Use separate monitoring-as-code stack

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance
findings.description: Infrastructure is fully defined as SAM/CloudFormation IaC. CI runs on push and pull_request. However, no drift detection is configured.
findings.gap: No drift detection. Manual changes would not be detected.
findings.recommendation: Add scheduled CloudFormation drift detection or AWS Config rules.

compensating_controls: Enable CloudFormation drift detection on a schedule
Add AWS Config rules

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: Three unit tests cover idempotency and scope denial for create_charge. No tests for refund_charge, no error response format tests, no edge case tests, no integration tests.
findings.gap: Limited test coverage — only happy path for create_charge and two error cases tested.
findings.recommendation: Expand test suite to cover refund_charge, validation errors (422), and edge cases. Add integration tests.

compensating_controls: Add pytest tests for refund_charge and validation errors
Add integration tests using sam local start-api

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: Charge and Refund records include created_at timestamps. The ledger is append-only. However, no data freshness signaling is implemented — no Cache-Control or ETag headers.
findings.gap: No freshness signaling. Agent cannot determine if GET response is authoritative or cached.
findings.recommendation: Add Cache-Control and/or ETag headers to GET responses.

compensating_controls: Add Cache-Control headers to GET responses
Add ETag/Last-Modified headers

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: Tests use a DynamoDB Local stub fixture. RUNBOOK references --config-env prod. No staging environment IaC, no docker-compose, no seed data in the repository.
findings.gap: No in-repo staging or sandbox environment definition.
findings.recommendation: Add samconfig.toml with dev/staging/prod configs and docker-compose.yml for local testing.

compensating_controls: Add samconfig.toml with environment configs
Add docker-compose.yml with DynamoDB Local

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: The system does not emit events or webhooks for state changes. All state is observable only via synchronous GET requests.
findings.gap: No asynchronous notification mechanism for state transitions.
findings.recommendation: Consider adding EventBridge event emission on charge and refund state transitions.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After) are returned in API responses. No rate limit documentation in OpenAPI spec.
findings.gap: Callers cannot discover or adapt to rate limits programmatically.
findings.recommendation: Add rate limit headers to responses and document limits in OpenAPI spec.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: System handles financial data. B1 (response scoping): CLEAR — sensitive fields excluded from responses. B2 (access differentiation): CLEAR — OAuth scopes separate read/write. B3 (formal classification): INFO — no classification tags or sensitivity annotations.
findings.gap: No formal data classification metadata on infrastructure resources.
findings.recommendation: Add data classification tags to DynamoDB table and S3 bucket resources.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Stage A: Yes (financial data). Stage B: B1 CLEAR, B2 CLEAR, B3 INFO. Overall: INFO.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 resolved to INFO because B1 (response scoping) and B2 (access differentiation) are both clear — the system properly filters sensitive fields from responses and differentiates access via scopes. Only B3 (formal classification metadata) is absent, which resolves to INFO.

b1.reasoning: Charge responses exclude payment source; only id/amount/currency/status/created_at returned

b2.reasoning: OAuth scopes differentiate payments:read from payments:write

b3.reasoning: No classification tags on DynamoDB table or S3 bucket

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data quality scores, completeness metrics, or data profiling. Append-only design prevents corruption by construction.
findings.gap: No explicit quality scoring or completeness monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Consider monitoring null rates on required fields as a lightweight quality signal.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer exists. The DynamoDB single-table design is documented only via code patterns.
findings.gap: No formal metadata layer describing data semantics.
findings.recommendation: Add a schema documentation file for the DynamoDB table structure.

evaluations.title: Documented API Interface
evaluations.reason: REST API documented via OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec serving as API Gateway definition body

evaluations.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
evaluations.reason: OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec exists, validated in CI, used as API Gateway definition

evaluations.title: Structured Error Responses
evaluations.reason: Error schema with code, message, correlation_id. Named responses for 409, 422, 404

evaluations.title: Idempotent Write Operations
evaluations.reason: Idempotency-Key required on all mutations with deduplication logic and conflict detection

evaluations.title: Structured Response Format
evaluations.reason: All responses use application/json with well-defined JSON schemas

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no operations >30s, Lambda timeout is 15s

evaluations.title: Machine Identity Authentication
evaluations.reason: OAuth2 client-credentials flow via Cognito with client_id attribution in authorizer context

evaluations.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
evaluations.reason: OAuth scopes (payments:read/write) and per-function IAM policies (DynamoDBWritePolicy/ReadPolicy)

evaluations.title: Action-Level Authorization
evaluations.reason: Action-level auth via _require_scope() enforcing payments:write for mutations, payments:read for reads

evaluations.title: Credential Management
evaluations.reason: No hardcoded credentials. Cognito via SAM Parameter. No .env files. No secrets in code.

evaluations.title: Compensation and Rollback
evaluations.reason: Architecture eliminates need: atomic operations, append-only ledger, refunds as compensation, idempotency prevents duplicates

evaluations.title: Queryable Current State
evaluations.reason: GET /charges/{chargeId} allows state inspection before action

evaluations.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
evaluations.reason: Lambda timeout (15s) + boto3 SDK retry + serverless isolation + managed DynamoDB provides adequate resilience

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no P0 priority specified

evaluations.title: Selective Query Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered — no list/query endpoints with unbounded results

evaluations.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
evaluations.reason: OpenAPI spec enforces additionalProperties:false, type constraints, patterns, min/max. API Gateway validates requests. Structured 422 responses.

evaluations.title: PII Redaction in Logs
evaluations.reason: Logs contain only correlation_id, client_id (machine), charge_id, reason (enum). No PII logged.

evaluations.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
evaluations.reason: All field names are human-readable and semantically clear: id, amount, currency, status, created_at, charge_id, reason

evaluations.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
evaluations.reason: X-Ray tracing active, structured JSON logging via Powertools, X-Correlation-Id propagated through request lifecycle

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: ChargeCreated custom metric published via Powertools Metrics namespace Payments

evaluations.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
evaluations.reason: CI validates OpenAPI spec syntax + runs behavioral API tests (pytest) + type checking (mypy)

evaluations.title: Rollback Capability
evaluations.reason: SAM deployment model supports rollback via artifact redeployment. Documented in RUNBOOK.

evaluations.title: Encryption at Rest
evaluations.reason: DynamoDB SSE enabled. S3 bucket uses aws:kms encryption with BucketKeyEnabled.

items.summary: Resolve blockers (immutable audit logging, data residency policy) and highest-priority safety risks (identity suspension, concurrency, rate limiting, HITL controls).
Address remaining safety risks (identity propagation, blast radius limits) and quality gaps (schema versioning, alerting, drift detection, freshness signaling, staging).
Improve test coverage, add event emission, rate limit headers, data classification tags, and data catalog.

recommended_actions.action: Implement immutable audit logging with S3 Object Lock
recommended_actions.rationale: BLOCKER: Agent write operations must be logged immutably for compliance and forensics.

recommended_actions.action: Document data residency policy and add agent data handling boundaries
recommended_actions.rationale: BLOCKER: Financial data requires explicit residency documentation for safe agent integration.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-client rate limiting via API Gateway UsagePlan
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents runaway agent loops from overwhelming the payments API.

recommended_actions.action: Fix concurrency race in idempotency check with DynamoDB ConditionExpression
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents duplicate charge creation from concurrent agent requests.

recommended_actions.action: Add dynamic deny-list to Lambda authorizer for agent suspension
recommended_actions.rationale: Enables immediate revocation of misbehaving agent identities.

recommended_actions.action: Implement pending state workflow for human-in-the-loop approval
recommended_actions.rationale: High-value payment operations should support human review before commitment.
